sentence: She is happy.
The tall boy runs fast.
I read a book.
She gave me a book.
I found the book useful.
The dog barked loudly.
My father is a doctor.
We watched the movie.
They elected him president.

The man who smiled left.

The woman whom we met yesterday is a scientist.

notes: where is a relative adverb; grew up is treated as the clause V under the approved convention.

sentence: When I arrived home, my mother was cooking dinner.
Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
If you study hard, you will improve.
Although he was tired, he continued working.
I will call you after I finish my homework.
I think that she is right.
What he said surprised everyone.
notes: What is the internal object of said and part of the full nominal-clause subject.

sentence: I know where she lives.
notes: where is an interrogative adverb, not an object inside the subordinate clause.

sentence: That he passed the exam is surprising.
She asked whether I was ready.
There are many books on the desk.
notes: Existential there is not the subject; the subject is many books.

sentence: There was a problem with the plan.
notes: Existential there is not S; with the plan is a postmodifier excluded from S.

sentence: It is important to learn English.
notes: It is the formal subject; to learn English is the notional subject.

sentence: It seems that he is honest.
notes: that he is honest is a content clause, not scored as main O or C.

sentence: It was difficult for me to answer.
notes: It is the formal subject; for me to answer is the notional subject.

sentence: She wants to become a doctor.
To read books is enjoyable.
He decided to leave early.
I enjoy playing tennis.
Swimming in the sea is fun.
notes: Entire gerund phrase including in the sea is selected as main S.

sentence: The girl sitting by the window is my sister.
The letter written in English was difficult.
She opened the door and entered the room.
notes: Two V spans and two O spans are selected separately, linked by and. The subject She is shared.

sentence: He is smart but sometimes careless.
notes: Two C spans smart and careless are selected separately; sometimes is excluded.

sentence: The book that my teacher recommended yesterday was surprisingly difficult to understand.
notes: Select only difficult as C; retain surprisingly difficult to understand as full complement phrase.
